components.note: 册 (book) — a bundle of bamboo slips
刂 (knife) — cutting text out of it

example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ nà tiáo xiāoxi shān le.
example.english: I deleted that message.
example.fact: 删 is the everyday verb for deleting files and messages: 删除 (delete), 删掉, 删减 (cut down). Its original sense was trimming bamboo-slip books with a knife.

components.note: An old character related to 乌 (crow), borrowed to write the preposition.

example.pinyin: Tā shēng yú Běijīng.
example.english: He was born in Beijing.
example.fact: 於 is the traditional-script form of 于, the literary preposition 'in, at, to'. In simplified text 于 is used instead, while 於 survives in traditional texts and some surnames (read Yū).

components.note: 亻 (person) — a helper
左 (zuǒ) gives the sound — an exact match; the left hand was the helping hand

example.hanzi: 这个数据可以佐证他的说法。
example.pinyin: Zhège shùjù kěyǐ zuǒzhèng tā de shuōfǎ.
example.english: This data supports what he says.
example.fact: 佐 is a bound form: 佐证 (corroborate), 辅佐 (assist), 佐料 (seasoning) and 佐餐 (to go with a meal).

components.note: 皿 (dish) — something valuable
次 (here the old drooling-mouth form) — coveting it

example.hanzi: 昨晚有人盗走了他的车。
example.pinyin: Zuówǎn yǒurén dàozǒu le tā de chē.
example.english: Someone stole his car last night.
example.fact: 盗 is bound: 盗版 (pirated), 盗窃 (theft), 强盗 (robber), 海盗 (pirate) and 被盗 (stolen, as in account hacking).

components.note: 氵 (water) — irrigation
夭 (yāo) offers a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Zhè piàn tǔdì fēicháng féiwò.
example.english: This land is very fertile.
example.fact: 沃 gives 肥沃 (fertile), 沃土 (rich soil), 沃野千里 and the store name 沃尔玛 (Walmart).

components.note: Simplified from 義 (sheep over 'I'); the modern shape is just 乂 with a dot, so it is learned as a whole.

example.hanzi: 他是一个很讲义气的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè hěn jiǎng yìqì de péngyou.
example.english: He's a friend who is very loyal.
example.fact: 义 is one of the Confucian virtues (仁义礼智信). 义气 is loyalty among friends, 意义 is meaning, 义工 is a volunteer, and 义父 an adoptive father.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — a landslide
朋 (péng) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Shān bēng le, lù bèi dǔzhù le.
example.english: The mountain collapsed and blocked the road.
example.fact: 崩 gives 崩溃 (to break down), 雪崩 (avalanche), 崩塌 (collapse). In modern speech 我崩溃了 means 'I'm losing it'. Historically it was used for the death of an emperor.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread) — weaving
只 (zhī) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Nǎinai zài zhī máoyī.
example.english: Grandma is knitting a sweater.
example.fact: 织 gives 织布 (weave cloth), 织毛衣 (knit a jumper), and 组织 (organisation, literally weave together). 织女 is the Weaver Girl in the Qixi legend.

components.note: 火 (fire) — the glow of fire, the core of 'red'; the top is traditionally read as 大 (big)

example.pinyin: Tā chìjiǎo zài shātān shang zǒu.
example.english: He walked barefoot on the beach.
example.fact: 赤 means red but is also 'bare': 赤脚 (barefoot), 赤字 (deficit, 'red figures'), 赤道 (the equator). 红 is the everyday red.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree, with a stroke on top marking the tip

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù páshān.
example.english: We're going hiking at the weekend.
example.fact: 末 gives 周末 (weekend), 月末 (end of the month), 末日 (doomsday) and 粉末 (powder). It is the tree's tip, the opposite of 本 (root).

components.note: 氵 (water) — rising water
张 (zhāng) gives the sound — differs in tone

example.pinyin: Zuìjìn càijià zhǎng le hěn duō.
example.english: Vegetable prices have gone up a lot lately.
example.fact: 涨 gives 涨价 (price increase) and 上涨 (rise). Read zhàng it means 'swell', as in 涨红了脸 ('face flushed').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — turning
另 (lìng) offers a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Nǐ zài qiánmiàn lùkǒu xiàng zuǒ guǎi.
example.english: Turn left at the junction ahead.
example.fact: 拐 gives directions: 左拐, 拐弯 (turn a corner). 拐杖 is a walking stick, and 拐骗 is to kidnap or swindle.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing
龙 (lóng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Tā de yéye ěrduo lóng le.
example.english: His grandfather has gone deaf.
example.fact: 聋 gives 聋哑 (deaf and mute) and 装聋作哑 ('pretend to be deaf and dumb'), meaning to feign ignorance.

components.note: Simplified from 廣; the modern 广 is an old 'building' radical shape, which is read yǎn as a radical.

example.pinyin: Tā de zhīshi miàn hěn guǎng.
example.english: He has wide-ranging knowledge.
example.fact: As a word, 广 (simplified from 廣) means wide: 广告 (advert), 广场 (square), 广泛 (widespread) and 广东 (Guangdong). As a character part, 广 is the 'cliff-house' radical read yǎn.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — wrapped in cloth
果 (guǒ) gives the sound — an exact match

example.hanzi: 她用毯子把孩子裹起来。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng tǎnzi bǎ háizi guǒ qǐlái.
example.english: She wrapped the child in a blanket.
example.fact: 裹 is in 包裹 (parcel), 裹挟 (to sweep along), 裹足不前 (hold back) and 裹腹 (to fill the stomach).

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person saving
诸 (zhū) offers a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Wǒ měi gè yuè dōu chǔ yìdiǎn qián.
example.english: I save a bit of money every month.
example.fact: 储 is a bound form: 储蓄 (savings), 储存 (store), 储备 (reserve), 存储 (storage) and 储物柜 (locker).

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — the body
中 (zhōng) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā de jiǎo zhǒng le.
example.english: His foot is swollen.
example.fact: 肿 gives 肿瘤 (tumour), 浮肿 (puffiness), 红肿 (red and swollen) and 肿胀.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — body tissue
莫 (mò) gives the sound — differs in tone

example.pinyin: Wǒ yòng miànmó hùfū.
example.english: I use a face mask for skincare.
example.fact: 膜 gives 面膜 (face mask), 薄膜 (thin film), 耳膜 (eardrum), 视网膜 (retina) and 保鲜膜 (cling film). 膜拜 now also means to adore someone.

components.note: 舌 (tongue) — speech
辛 (bitter, harsh) — hard words, declining

example.pinyin: Tā cízhí le.
example.english: He resigned.
example.fact: 辞 is formal: 辞职 (resign), 辞退 (dismiss), 告辞 (take leave), 辞典 (dictionary), 不辞而别 (leave without saying goodbye). Compare 词 (word).

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the old sense was the twang of a drawn bow, which suggests expansiveness

example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng hóngyáng Zhōngguó wénhuà.
example.english: He wants to promote Chinese culture.
example.fact: 弘 is formal: 弘扬 (promote), 弘大 (grand). It is interchangeable with 宏 in some words, and appears in names such as 弘一法师.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — a bird
我 (wǒ) gives the sound — close to é

example.pinyin: Hébiān yǒu jǐ zhī bái é.
example.english: There are a few white geese by the river.
example.fact: The measure word is 只. 鹅 is the subject of the famous children's poem 《咏鹅》 'é, é, é', traditionally attributed to Luo Binwang at the age of seven.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — a plant
每 (měi) gives the sound — differs in the tone

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī cǎoméi.
example.english: I like eating strawberries.
example.fact: 莓 is bound: 草莓 (strawberry), 蓝莓 (blueberry), 树莓 (raspberry).

components.note: A standing person with two dots at the armpits — the original graph for 腋 (armpit), later borrowed for 'also'.

example.hanzi: 他是我的老师，亦是我的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de lǎoshī, yì shì wǒ de péngyou.
example.english: He is my teacher and also my friend.
example.fact: 亦 is literary for 也. In 亦师亦友 ('both teacher and friend') it forms a handy pattern. 不亦乐乎 ('isn't that a joy?') is now also used to mean 'extremely', as in 忙得不亦乐乎.

components.note: 王 (jade) — gems
林 (lín) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Wǒ péngyou jiào Línlin.
example.english: My friend is called Linlin.
example.fact: 琳 is used mostly in names and in 琳琅满目 (a dazzling array of treasures) from 'fine jade'.

excludeSuggestion: mostly appears in given names and the idiom 琳琅满目

components.note: 礻 (spirit, omen) — fortune and misfortune
呙 (guō) offers a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Jiǔ hòu kāichē huì chuǎnghuò.
example.english: Driving after drinking will cause a disaster.
example.fact: 祸 gives 车祸 (car accident), 闯祸 (cause trouble), 祸不单行 (misfortunes never come singly) and 祸从口出 (disaster comes from the mouth).

components.note: 比 (bǐ) gives a rough sound hint; the other part is a simplification of the old shape

example.pinyin: Tā jīnnián dàxué bìyè.
example.english: He's graduating from university this year.
example.fact: 毕 gives 毕业 (graduate), 毕竟 (after all), 完毕 (complete) and 毕生 (a whole lifetime). It's also a surname.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort
工 (gōng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Zhè cì shíyàn chénggōng le.
example.english: This experiment succeeded.
example.fact: 功 gives 成功 (succeed), 功夫 (kung fu, and also time or effort), 功劳 (credit), 功能 (function) and 气功 (qigong).

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — layered robes, extended to 'following' and 'continuing'
龙 (lóng) is a simplified stand-in for the old top, not a sound hint

example.pinyin: Táifēng xíjī le yánhǎi dìqū.
example.english: The typhoon struck the coastal areas.
example.fact: 袭 gives 袭击 (attack, also for storms), 偷袭 (sneak attack), 空袭 (air raid), 世袭 (hereditary) and 抄袭 (plagiarise).

components.note: 大 (big) — grand claims
亏 (kuī) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī kuā wǒ xiě de hǎo.
example.english: The teacher praised my writing.
example.fact: 夸 means both 'praise' (夸奖) and 'exaggerate' (夸张, 夸大). 夸 someone is the ordinary way to compliment them.

components.note: The origin is debated, usually explained as someone hiding or vanishing, which fits 'flee, lose, die'.

example.hanzi: 这场事故造成两人死亡。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng shìgù zàochéng liǎng rén sǐwáng.
example.english: The accident caused two deaths.
example.fact: 亡 gives 死亡 (death), 逃亡 (flee), 灭亡 (perish) and 亡羊补牢 ('mend the pen after the sheep are lost', better late than never). Don't mix it up with 忙 (busy) and 忘 (forget).

components.note: 犭 (animal) — early Chinese writing used animal radicals for outside peoples; the 火 on the right has lost any sound link

example.pinyin: Dí Rénjié shì Tángcháo de míngchén.
example.english: Di Renjie was a famous Tang dynasty official.
example.fact: 狄 was an ancient name for northern peoples, and is mostly seen as a surname: 狄仁杰 ('Detective Dee'). It also appears in transliteration, as in 狄更斯 (Dickens).

excludeSuggestion: mostly a surname or in transliterations

components.note: 女 (woman) — a woman; it also gives the sound
又 (hand) — seized by a hand

example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng zuò jīnqián de núlì.
example.english: He doesn't want to be a slave to money.
example.fact: 奴 gives 奴隶 (slave), 奴才 (lackey), 农奴 (serf). Modern slang uses it for people tied down: 房奴 (mortgage slave).

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquid
发 (fā) gives a rough sound hint

example.pinyin: Bié wǎng dì shang pō shuǐ.
example.english: Don't splash water on the ground.
example.fact: 泼 gives 泼水节 (the Water-Splashing Festival), 泼冷水 ('to pour cold water', as in English) and 活泼 (lively).

components.note: Hands lifting something up in offering, the old picture of presenting with both hands.

example.pinyin: Tā fèngmìng qù Běijīng kāihuì.
example.english: He went to Beijing for a meeting by order.
example.fact: 奉 is formal: 奉献 (dedicate), 奉命 (by order), 奉承 (flatter) and 信奉 (to believe in). 无可奉告 is the official 'no comment'.

components.note: 穴 (hole) — sneaking in through a hole
切 (qiè) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu qièzǒu le tā de qiánbāo.
example.english: The thief stole his wallet.
example.fact: 窃 gives 盗窃 (theft), 窃听 (eavesdrop), 窃取 (steal), 窃笑 (snicker) and 窃喜 (secretly pleased).

components.note: 木 (wood) — a wooden stick
昆 (kūn) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā shǒu lǐ ná zhe yì gēn mùgùn.
example.english: He is holding a wooden stick.
example.fact: The measure word is 根. 光棍 ('bare stick') means a bachelor, and 光棍节 is Singles' Day on 11 November, with its four 'sticks'. 恶棍 is a villain.

components.note: 厂 (cover) — a shield or screen
目 (eye) — an eye peering from behind it

example.hanzi: 战士举起盾牌挡住了箭。
example.pinyin: Zhànshì jǔ qǐ dùnpái dǎngzhù le jiàn.
example.english: The soldier raised his shield and blocked the arrow.
example.fact: 盾 is in 盾牌 (shield) and 矛盾 ('spear and shield', contradiction). The idiom 自相矛盾 is from a story of a seller who claimed both unbreakable. Also a currency, as in 越南盾.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the one who speaks for the family
儿 (legs, a person) — a figure standing

example.hanzi: 他们兄弟两个长得很像。
example.pinyin: Tāmen xiōngdì liǎng gè zhǎng de hěn xiàng.
example.english: The two brothers look very alike.
example.fact: 兄 is more formal than 哥. 兄弟 means brothers and is also a friendly address ('bro'); 老兄 is 'mate'. Also 兄长 (elder brother, respectful).

components.note: 女 (woman) — a woman
彐 (hand) — the remnant of the hand holding a broom in the older 婦

example.hanzi: 这位妇女是我们的邻居。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi fùnǚ shì wǒmen de línjū.
example.english: This woman is our neighbour.
example.fact: 妇 gives 妇女 (women, formal, as in 妇女节 on 8 March), 媳妇 (wife, daughter-in-law), 夫妇 (married couple) and 妇科 (gynaecology).

components.note: 戈 (halberd) — a weapon that cuts

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè zhāng tú jié xiàlái.
example.english: Please take a screenshot of this picture.
example.fact: 截 gives 截图 (screenshot), 截止 (cut-off date), 截然不同 (sharply different). It is also a measure word for sections: 一截绳子.
